section_summary: This section documents the development and internal U.S. interagency debate regarding policy for the replacement of cultural objects looted or destroyed by Japan during its military aggression in World War II. It centers on proposed State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee (SWNCC/SANACC) and Far Eastern Commission (FEC) policies to provide claimant Allied nations, particularly China, with approximately equivalent cultural property from Japanese public institutions and convicted war criminals. The documents capture sharp disagreement between the Department of State, which favored an early and moderate replacement program, and the Department of the Army (Civil Affairs Division) and SCAP, who opposed the policy on grounds of administrative burden, currency inflation, precedent, and potential loss of Japanese goodwill.

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum transmitting a proposed policy statement regarding the replacement of cultural objects lost or destroyed during Japanese aggression.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a proposed policy statement on the replacement of cultural objects looted or wantonly destroyed by Japan during its period of aggression for consideration by the SWNCC Subcommittee for the Far East. The policy proposes that claimant Allied nations receive cultural objects of equivalent value from Japanese public institutions or confiscated private property, while excluding Japanese National Treasures and items essential to SCAP's democratization and education programs. Appendices summarize historical precedents, Japanese laws preserving National Treasures, and preliminary discussions in the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Proposed Policy Statement on Replacement of Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: Memorandum analyzing arguments for and against the proposed cultural objects replacement policy for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes arguments for and against the cultural replacement policy, rebutting Army Department objections regarding Japanese goodwill and administrative difficulty, and recommends holding the paper in the Far East Subcommittee until George F. Kennan returns.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) (SANACC 385 and SFE 202 Series)

subfiles.about: Subcommittee paper circulating a memorandum by the Civil Affairs Division member opposing the cultural objects replacement policy.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a memorandum by the CAD member opposing the replacement policy due to fears of alienating Japanese goodwill, administrative difficulty, and currency inflation, and recommending submitting divergent State and Army views to SANACC.
subfiles.title: SFE 202/2: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan)
subfiles.to: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East

subfiles.about: SANACC paper circulating a State Department study on the replacement of cultural objects lost or destroyed as a consequence of Japanese aggression.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a State Department study proposing U.S. policy for requiring Japan to replace cultural objects wantonly destroyed or lost from Allied territories during Japanese military aggression. Claims would be satisfied through approximately equivalent objects from Japanese public institutions or war criminals' confiscated property, excluding National Treasures and items required for occupation democratization. Appendices provide background on wartime Allied restitution principles, Japanese cultural preservation laws, and Far Eastern Commission deliberations.
subfiles.title: SANACC 385: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan)

subfiles.about: SANACC paper circulating SCAP's recommendation to defer the replacement of cultural objects until the peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a radiogram from SCAP Tokyo recommending that the replacement of cultural objects be deferred until the Japanese peace treaty is signed and then administered by an international tribunal of specialists.
subfiles.title: SANACC 385/1: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan)

subfiles.about: Subcommittee paper circulating a Civil Affairs Division memorandum recommending the withdrawal of SANACC 385.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a memorandum by the CAD member recommending the withdrawal of SANACC 385 because it burdens SCAP, risks alienating Japanese goodwill, and sets an undesirable precedent for broader restitution in kind.
subfiles.title: SFE 202: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan)
subfiles.to: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East

subfiles.about: Subcommittee paper circulating revised conclusions by the State Department restricting cultural replacement to objects that served public cultural purposes.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a memorandum and revised conclusions from the State Department Member amending SANACC 385 in light of Far Eastern Commission discussions. The revision restricts eligible replacement claims to cultural objects that had previously served public cultural purposes, such as in public libraries and museums. It also expands protection for Japanese cultural heritage by explicitly exempting early temple complexes, including the Nara Complex.
subfiles.title: SFE 202/1: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan)
subfiles.to: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East

subfiles.about: Memorandum suggesting asking Chinese representatives for specific details regarding their library replacement requests.
subfiles.summary: Advises indicating sympathy in principle to anticipated Chinese representations while pressing them for precise details on specific libraries and the scale of replacement desired.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) (SANACC 385 and SFE 202 Series)

subfiles.about: Memorandum reporting on Chinese Embassy plans to approach the State Department regarding cultural object replacements.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Chinese diplomats will approach the Department regarding cultural replacements, outlines anticipated Chinese arguments and concerns over FEC draft restrictions, and urges prompt SANACC policy approval.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: Foreign broadcast monitoring report on Chinese requests for the return of cultural objects taken by Japan since 1895.
subfiles.summary: Monitored Nanking radio report on Chinese demands for the return of antiquities taken by Japan since 1895, SCAP's restrictive reporting orders, and Chinese cultural loss statistics.
subfiles.title: Chinese Antiquities

subfiles.about: Memorandum analyzing the Far Eastern Commission stalemate and refuting Army objections to the cultural replacement program.
subfiles.summary: Reviews the diplomatic history in the FEC and SANACC, systematically refutes the CAD member's five objections to the cultural replacement program, and recommends submitting a split report to SANACC.
subfiles.title: State Department Position on SFE 202/2, "Replacement of Cultural Objects"

subfiles.about: Memorandum providing background on FEC deliberations and explaining the purpose of proposed cables to Tokyo and Nanking.
subfiles.summary: Provides background on the FEC stalemate, representations by Ambassador Wellington Koo, and doubts raised by Verner Clapp, explaining that attached queries to Tokyo and Nanking will clarify key factual unknowns.
subfiles.title: Dispatch of Attached Messages

subfiles.about: Draft telegram requesting SCAP's estimates of Japanese art objects eligible for removal under proposed cultural replacement policies.
subfiles.summary: Informs SCAP that diplomatic pressure from China and the Far Eastern Commission necessitates resolving the cultural replacement policy before a peace treaty. Details the competing majority and minority FEC policy proposals along with Ambassador Wellington Koo's suggested compromise on public accessibility. Requests SCAP provide estimates of the quantity and value of Japanese cultural objects eligible for removal under these proposals.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram (or Airmail Letter) to SCAP (through Army)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Draft telegram querying SCAP on the volume of Japanese art objects eligible for removal under replacement proposals.
subfiles.summary: Draft telegram querying SCAP regarding the quantity and value of Japanese art objects subject to removal under majority and minority FEC replacement proposals, noting Ambassador Koo's compromise and Hu Shih's microfilm suggestion.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram to SCAP (through Army)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Draft telegram querying Embassy Nanking on Chinese cultural losses, public interest in replacement, and reaction to Hu Shih's microfilming proposal.
subfiles.summary: Queries Embassy Nanking regarding the actual extent of Chinese cultural destruction, Chinese public and scholarly interest in replacement, ability to substantiate claims, and reaction to Hu Shih's microfilming proposal.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram to Nanking

subfiles.about: Memorandum discussing policy timing following George F. Kennan's return and noting Chinese interest in microfilms.
subfiles.summary: Notes that Kennan's report favors resolving cultural replacements before the peace treaty, and urges obtaining precise details on Chinese library losses and Hu Shih's microfilm proposal.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) (SANACC 385 and SFE 202 Series)

subfiles.about: Memorandum conveying Chinese Affairs Division concurrence with Robert A. Fearey's analysis and urging a compromise between Chinese demands and SCAP's position.
subfiles.summary: States Chinese Affairs Division concurrence with Fearey's memorandum, urging a compromise between China's excessive claims dating to 1895 and SCAP's exaggerated concern over Japanese goodwill.
subfiles.title: Replacement of Lost Cultural Objects

subfiles.about: Memorandum reporting on Far Eastern Commission Reparations Committee debates over Japanese technical information and cultural object replacement.
subfiles.summary: Reports to General McCoy on FEC Reparations Committee debates over Japanese technical information and cultural replacement, including U.S. rebuttals of Netherlands accusations and clarifications regarding Italian Treaty precedents.
subfiles.title: Reparations Committee Meeting of 11 February 1948

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of SFE 202 circulating a CAD memorandum recommending withdrawal of SANACC 385.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of SFE 202 (Copy No. 18), circulating a CAD memorandum recommending that SANACC 385 be withdrawn to avoid burdening SCAP and alienating Japanese goodwill.
subfiles.title: SFE 202: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) [Duplicate]
subfiles.to: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of SANACC 385/1 circulating SCAP's recommendation to defer cultural replacement to the peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of SANACC 385/1 (Copy No. 56), circulating SCAP's recommendation to defer cultural replacement claims to the peace treaty for adjudication by an international specialist tribunal.
subfiles.title: SANACC 385/1: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) [Duplicate]

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of SFE 202/2 circulating a CAD memorandum opposing cultural replacement proposals.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of SFE 202/2 (Copy No. 22), circulating a CAD memorandum recommending that split State and Army views on cultural replacement be submitted to SANACC for resolution.
subfiles.title: SFE 202/2: Replacement of Cultural Objects (Japan) [Duplicate]
subfiles.to: State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East

subfiles.summary: Office note inquiring whether Hamilton wants more information regarding Barnett's memorandum referenced in item one.
